raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t chase fancy things. On my 10.1 mu, I’ll still do what has kept the family steady: wheat-maize on the better land, and cotton on the rest. Wheat and maize turn fast here, and even if one side is not perfect, at least there are two harvests. Cotton takes more watching and more hand labor, but if the price is decent it still brings cash. Some people in my family work outside, so I cannot make a plan that needs too much labor at one time. I also have a well, so if spring is dry or the wheat is thirsty, I can give water, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water more than needed.

For wheat, I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because if wheat turns yellow later, yield drops and then saving a little money is not worth it. Maize after wheat has to be planted quickly, so I’ll keep land preparation simple and get it in fast. Cotton I’ll keep on a smaller piece, because it needs more hands and I cannot manage too much of it at my age. I mostly follow what worked on my own fields and what nearby farmers do, maybe adjusting a little if prices or weather look different.
